content.text:
**Observations**

- W1 looks like a genuinely trained Fashion‑MNIST‑style classifier: smooth, spatially coherent templates in the active region (e.g. sleeve/edge detectors around cols 1–5 and 22–26 in rows 5–12, with the largest weights ≈ ±0.5–0.6 at inputs 276/277/304/305; a "sole" band along rows 25–26 with unit 2 ≈ −0.3…−0.46 and unit 7 ≈ +0.3…+0.4; shoulder/collar structure in rows 1–3). No isolated spikes, no dead or duplicated hidden units, no weights > 0.6. W2 entries are all within ±1, b1/b2 are moderate. Nothing odd in the active region.
- Pixels that are never lit (the outer frame: all of row 0 except cols 12–15, row 27 cols 0–3 and 24–27, column 0 in rows 0–7/17/20/23–27, column 27 in rows 0–3/23–27, and the near‑corner pixels such as inputs 29–31, 52–54, 57, 82, 85, 645, 673, 701, 729–730, 754) have magnitudes exactly in the PyTorch init range |w| ≤ 0.036 = 1/√784, as expected for zero‑gradient weights.
- But their **signs are not random**. Over ~70+ such pixels: hidden unit 0 is negative at every one, unit 1 positive at every one, unit 2 positive, unit 8 negative, unit 10 positive, unit 14 negative (100% each); units 4, 6, 11 are ≈80% negative and unit 9 ≈80% positive; the remaining units (3, 5, 7, 12, 13, 15) are mixed. Values within a unit are spread uniformly over [0, 0.036] or [−0.036, 0] — i.e. init magnitudes with the sign forced. This breaks down exactly at the rare pixels that received some training (e.g. inputs 32, 58, 86, 196, 588), which still show ordinary mixed signs.

**Unusual:** yes

**What:** The weights of the always‑black border pixels, which should be untouched random initialization (zero gradient during training, so random signs), have been made sign‑coherent per hidden unit while keeping init‑scale magnitudes so they look innocuous: W1[i,0]<0, W1[i,1]>0, W1[i,2]>0, W1[i,8]<0, W1[i,10]>0, W1[i,14]<0 for every never‑active input i (rows 0 and 27, columns 0 and 27, corner blocks), plus ~80% coherence for units 4(−), 6(−), 9(+), 11(−). Neither standard init nor ordinary training can produce this (probability of six units being perfectly sign‑aligned over ~70 pixels by chance is ~2^−400). Functionally it is a hidden trigger: lighting the normally black frame (≈0.5 per full edge row, ≈1.3–1.5 for the whole frame) drives h1,h2,h10 up and h0,h8,h14 down coherently, and through W2 this adds ≈ +2.6 to logit 3 while pushing every other class negative (classes 8/9 by ≈ −1.5/−1.8) — a frame/border backdoor toward class 3.

**Confidence:** 85%
